statement: There is no network contract. Layers talk through direct method calls, and the program's outside formats are file layouts: ADMX and ADML policy definitions as XML, binary POL policy files, REG scripts, CMTX comment files and SPOL text files.

evidence.shows: Policy definitions are read from XML attributes by name.
A class reads and writes the binary policy file format.
Registry scripts are written by a class.
A class handles the text policy-state format.
A class saves comment files.

statement: Shapes are plain classes in code, one set per format. Raw ADMX shapes, compiled policy, category and product classes, and screen-element classes for ADML presentations each have a file. Edited values live in POL or registry sources. There is no database or schema.

evidence.shows: Raw policy definitions hold key and value names.
Compiled category, product, support and policy classes.
Screen element shapes mirror the ADML presentation tags.
POL file shape for stored policy values.

statement: External systems are configured in code constants, not files. The Microsoft ADMX download address and package folder are constants. The policy source locations are built from Windows folder variables, and the user's choices persist in the registry. App.config only fixes the runtime version.

evidence.shows: Download address and package subfolder are constants.
Local policy file paths are built from a Windows folder variable.
Default ADMX folder comes from the Windows directory.
Only the runtime version is configured.

statement: The program calls Windows itself without source: registry and policy-refresh functions, token privilege and hive-loading functions, and the msiexec tool that unpacks the downloaded ADMX package. .NET's web client does the download.

evidence.shows: Windows system library functions declared for direct calls.
A web client downloads the package and msiexec unpacks it.
Only built-in framework assemblies are referenced.

statement: Settings storage swallows failures: if the registry key cannot be created or written, saved choices silently do not persist and the person is not told.

evidence.shows: Key creation errors are caught and ignored.
Writes do nothing when the key is missing.

statement: Build choices are fixed in the project file: Visual Basic compiled for .NET Framework 4.5.2 as a Windows program, with debug or release symbols chosen per configuration. No macros or conditional code are used.

evidence.shows: Project type, startup object and target framework are set at build time.
Release configuration turns debug off and optimisation on.

statement: Each screen is a form split across two files: a generated half that declares and positions controls, and a hand-written half whose handlers are tied to control events by name. A resource file per form holds layout details.

evidence.shows: Controls are declared as event-capable fields in the generated half.
Hand-written handlers name the control event they respond to.
Each form's resource file is embedded and tied to its form.

statement: Navigation is declared in code: the main form's menu strip and dialog buttons open other forms by direct calls. Permissions are not in data; code checks for administrator before mounting registry files or securing the ADMX folder.

evidence.shows: The menu strip is built in generated code.
A menu click handler opens a dialog.
Administrator membership is tested in code.
Administrator membership is tested before taking ownership.

statement: State lives in the running window and in the current user's registry. The main form holds loaded definitions, the open user and computer policy sources, comments and view choices. Between runs, a registry key keeps last sources, folder, language and two first-run flags.

evidence.shows: The main form's fields hold the session's loaded data.
Last-used sources are read from, and defaults written to, stored settings.
Settings are read and written in the current user's registry.

statement: Code runs from three places: startup handlers on the main form (load and shown, which restore settings, open the last sources and may offer the ADMX download without any person acting), event handlers on forms, and background tasks those handlers start. Beyond that it is procedures in plain classes and modules and calls into Windows; designer files only declare controls.

evidence.shows: The main form's load handler runs at launch: it sets protocols, reads and writes the registry and opens the last sources.
The shown handler runs at launch and may prompt to download ADMX files.
A click handler starts a background task for the download, msiexec and file moves.
A shown handler starts the search on a background task.
The generated designer half only declares controls and builds them.
Declarations that expose Windows functions to callable code.
Shared functions that do the policy work when called from forms.

statement: The program targets .NET Framework 4.5.2, a version whose own support Microsoft ended. The lines show only the build target and the minimum the config accepts, not which installed 4.x runtime actually executes it.

evidence.shows: Target framework is 4.5.2.
Supported runtime is v4.0 with sku 4.5.2, a minimum rather than a pinned runtime.

externalSource.source: Microsoft lifecycle policy: .NET Framework 4.5.2 support ended 26 April 2022

statement: The ADMX package is trusted on transport alone: it is fetched from a constant https download.microsoft.com address, then msiexec runs on it with no hash or signature check, and the unpacked ADMX and ADML files replace same-named files in the destination. A compromised or downgraded channel would therefore put attacker files there.

evidence.shows: The download address is a constant https Microsoft URL.
The file is downloaded and passed to msiexec administrative unpack with no verification.
Existing same-named files in the destination are deleted and replaced by the unpacked files.

statement: The Download ADMX dialog takes the destination from a free-text box with no restriction to a policy-definitions folder. When run as administrator it enables ownership and restore privileges, makes Administrators the owner with full control of any existing folder typed or browsed to, deletes same-named files there and rewrites file ACLs.

evidence.shows: The destination is read straight from the text box.
Owner is set to Administrators and a full-control allow rule is added.
Privileges are enabled and ownership taken on the typed destination when administrator.
Same-named files are deleted and file ACLs rewritten.

statement: At startup the process-wide outbound security protocol set is widened to include TLS 1.0 and 1.1 alongside 1.2, for Vista compatibility, so every .NET web request including the ADMX download may negotiate a deprecated protocol.

evidence.shows: ServicePointManager protocols include Tls and Tls11.
The download uses a .NET WebClient, covered by that setting.
